newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The National Bank is introducing a new policy on interest rates, offering cheaper loans to private and business clients. Working capital will be up to 2.0 percent cheaper with the floor rate set at 12.0 percent. The cuts - of up to 3.0 percent - will also apply to credit card loans.

--Deputy Finance Minister George Drys yesterday raised the issue of the need to reduce the high tax rate for businesses, during his meeting with Greek and US businessmen. Drys admitted the tax rate was one of the highest in Europe, in contrast to tax rates for individuals, one of the lowest.

--How to strengthen the social state, speed up development and create new jobs will be the focus of the European socialist finance ministers meeting organised for Athens this weekend. Prime Minister Costas Simitis and National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou will host the meeting.

--The business world is expected to react strongly to a recent decision by Drys to increase certain indices used to calculate the tax bracket that firms fall into. The move is expected to bring increased taxes for upwards of 600,000 businesses and self-employed professionals subject to the "objective tax" criteria.
--Former European Commission president Jacques Delors will be in Athens tomorrow for the European socialist finance ministers meeting, which will look at how Europe can best fund growth.

--The finance ministry is examining a partial index-linking of the tax scale as well as an adjustment in the tax scale itself, bringing the number of brackets down from five to four. The measures will be up for discussion with unions and employers' groups in July.
--The development ministry is working on how to protect prices given that retailers are beginning to offer sales and discounts year-round, directly undermining the institution of seasonal sales.

--Drys said yesterday that the government was working on a package of measures of tax incentives designed to lure foreign investment capital and to create strong and independent Greek firms. "Tax and fiscal policies are the keys to economic growth," he said.
--National Bank announced an increase in profits of 89 percent in the first five months of this year, compared to the same period last year.

--There are changes expected in the status of business premises, including increased compensation for those evicted and possible renegotiation of rentals. The measures, promoted by the development ministry, will have no adverse effect on plans for a full deregulation by September 1. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
